newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Nov 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Nov 26.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company -- CLARKE HEADS OFF TORY REVOLT

In an address to the Commons on Monday afternoon the chancellor Kenneth Clarke assured MPs that he would enter into no binding agreements at next weekend's meeting in Dublin of EU finance ministers. The assurance was given to MPs after considerable political furor over the initial refusal by the Prime Minister to countenance the holding of a Commons debate on Emu prior to the December summit on the issue in Dublin. Clarke also stressed his determination to resist the UK's being the target for EU financial control even if it remains outside the single currency.
-- SALVESEN TO DEMERGE HIRE UNIT

PLans have been unveiled by Christian Salvesen to demerge its Aggreko hire division and to distribute among shareholders around 150 million stg. However, the break-up plans have been attacked as a financial "sleight of hand" by former chairman and chief executive Sir Gerald Elliot. The break-up plans, prompted by a takeover bid for the company in June by Hays, were unveiled at the same time as a rise in first half pre-tax profits of 14.7 percent to 51.6 million stg.
-- LIRA RISES AGAINST MARK AFTER RETURN TO THE ERM

On the day of its return to the ERM the Italian lira rose in value against the German mark. The market judged that Italy would be able to maintain its currency at above the 990 level at which it returned to the exchange rate system for at least a number of months. However, if the country fails to keep the lira within a 2.2 percent band in relation to the mark for two years Italian hopes of participating in the single currency will once more come under pressure.
-- CREST WILL KEEP TO ORIGINAL TIMETABLE

The electronic share settlement system, Crest, has announced it will as planned be fully operational by the spring of 1997. There had been some concerns about the switch from the paper-based system Talisman after a series of technical problems with Crest. However, CrestCo, the company running Crest, has received temporary clearance from City regulators who will monitor the system's progress closely. Already a switch by 17 large companies to Crest has been postponed, easing the strain on the system for now.
-- EUROTUNNEL HIT BY FEARS ON PAYMENTS

Shares in Eurotunnel fell amid speculation that the company will be obliged to pay considerable sums in compensation to the three national railways that operate the Eurostar passenger service which has been interrupted as a result of the recent fire. There have been suggestions that these payments could reach some 10 million stg. The company has also announced that it is to cease making predictions as to when it expects to resume passenger services through the tunnel.
-- STRONG POUND 'THREATENS HOLLYWOOD'S INVESTMENT'

There is concern that the recent rise in sterling against the US dollar could act as a deterrent to Hollywood companies proceeding with production work in the UK. One of the main attractions of Britain for US film producers has been its low costs, and of late there has been a sharp rise in the number of movies being shot in the UK. However, a recent report highlights the fact that the appreciation of sterling has led to the UK becoming less expensive for film production than the US in only two of seven key cost components.
-- BABCOCK SECURES ONE BLN STG OF ORDERS IN ROSYTH DEAL

It has been agreed that engineering group Babcock International will acquire the Rosyth Dockyard in Scotland for between 20 million and 25 million stg. The deal comes after the company secured orders from the Ministry of Defence for ship refits worth in the region of one billion stg. It is believed the price paid for the yard is about 30 percent below the level originally agreed. The defence secretary has estimated the privatisation will result in the government saving in the region of 100 million stg over ten years.
-- ROSYTH STAFF TO GET ONE-OFF PAYMENTS IN SELL-OFF

The government's decision to sell the Rosyth dockyard to engineering group Babcock will result in staff at the facility receiving one-off payments of about 15,000 stg. The money will compensate staff for their surrender of public sector redundancy rights. This issue had proved a considerable stumbling block in attempts to reach agreement on the sale of the facility.
Existing orders from the MoD are expected to keep the yard operating at its present capacity for about five years.
-- TARGET FOR NEW HOMES ON URBAN LAND 'TOO LOW'

The government has signalled its intention of increasing by at least 20 percent the target for the proportion of new homes to be built on former industrial and urban land - brownfield sites - over the next 20 years. At present the target for the proportion of the 4.4 million new homes is 50 percent, a figure now described as inappropriate. The new targets have been welcomed by local authorities as well as environmentalists, though analysts are skeptical as to whether they can actually be achieved.
